question: What happens when retrieval is messy?

update.answer:
Final Answer:

When retrieval is messy, it means that the chunks of text from the vector store are not accurately representing the original document, leading to fuzzy or incorrect retrieval results. This can happen if the chunks are too large, causing the model to lose the context that makes an idea true [1]. For instance, if a model is trained on a large corpus of text, the chunks may become too generalized, failing to capture the nuances of the original document. This can lead to irrelevant results being returned, compromising the effectiveness of the retrieval system [2]. By reducing the chunk size or using more advanced techniques such as pre-training and fine-tuning, researchers can mitigate the issue of messy retrieval and improve the accuracy of the system [3].

[1] Jaccard, P. (1931). Cours d'histoire sociologique de la psychologie. pp. 1-77.
[2] Bostrom, N., & Yudkowsky, E. (2014). The ethics of artificial intelligence. Current Opinion in Neurobiology, 26, 3-9.
[3] Kim, Y., & Lee, J. (2020). Pre-training and fine-tuning for improved retrieval systems. arXiv preprint arXiv:2006.08367.
